Rashi on Pesachim 5a:10:1.hebrew: התם נמי - גבי לולב, ה' דהראשון למה לי:
Rashi on Pesachim 5a:10:1.english: There too - With regard to lulav, why do I need the [letter] hei of harishon?

Rashi on Pesachim 5a:11:1.hebrew: מראשון ושמיני נפקא - מדכתיב בהנהו שבתון, מכלל דאינך לאו שבתון נינהו:
Rashi on Pesachim 5a:11:1.english: Is derived from "first" and "eighth" - Since it is written regarding those [days] "a solemn rest," by implication the others are not "a solemn rest."

Rashi on Pesachim 5a:12:1.hebrew: על ענין ראשון - על ימים הקדומים לו, דהיינו חולו של מועד:
Rashi on Pesachim 5a:12:1.english: To the previous matter - To the days preceding it, that is, the intermediate days of the Festival.

Rashi on Pesachim 5a:13:1.hebrew: לא לכתוב רחמנא לא וי"ו - דמשמע ריבויא, דתו איצטריך ה"א למיעוט:
Rashi on Pesachim 5a:13:1.english: Let the Merciful One not write a vav - Which implies inclusion, such that a heh was then needed for exclusion.

Rashi on Pesachim 5a:14:1.hebrew: אלא מהני שלשה ראשון - דכתיב במקרא קודש דפסח, ומקרא קודש דסוכות, ומצות לולב — לא תותב לרב נחמן; דהני ראשון דכתיב בהו לאו למשמעותייהו קאתו, אלא שמא בעלמא הוא דנקראו ראשון, וכתנא דבי ר' ישמעאל:
Rashi on Pesachim 5a:14:1.english: Rather, from these three [occurrences of] rishon - Which are written regarding the sacred convocation of Passover, the sacred convocation of Sukkot, and the mitzvah of lulav — do not raise an objection against Rav Naḥman; for these [instances of the word] rishon written in them do not come for their [usual] meaning, but rather it is merely a name by which they are called rishon, and [this is] in accordance with the tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael.

Rashi on Pesachim 5a:14:2.hebrew: בשכר ג' ראשון - שביתת הרגל דפסח, ושביתת הרגל דחג, ונטילת לולב, שנקראו ראשונים — זכו לשלשה ראשון:
Rashi on Pesachim 5a:14:2.english: In reward for three [times] rishon - [In reward for] the cessation of work on the Festival of Passover, and the cessation of work on the Festival [of Sukkot], and the taking of the lulav, which were called “firsts” — they merited three [matters called] rishon.

Rashi on Pesachim 5a:16:1.hebrew: לא תשחט על חמץ וגו' - ושחיטת פסח זמנה מתחלת שבע, שהוא בין הערבים, שכבר נוטה חמה לצד שקיעתה. והכי אמרינן בפ' אמר להן הממונה (יומא כח:): צלותיה דאברהם מכי משחרי כותלי, דהיינו מחצות ואילך, וגמרינן מינה דשחיטת התמיד מתחלת שבע. וקשיא לן התם מתני' דתמיד נשחט בשש שעות ומחצה, ומשני לן: שאני כותלי בית המקדש דלא מכווני — רחבין תחתיהן מאד — ולא משתחרי עד שש ומחצה:
Rashi on Pesachim 5a:16:1.english: “You shall not slaughter over leaven,” etc. - And the slaughter of the Paschal offering, its time is from the beginning of the seventh [hour], which is “in the afternoon” [bein ha’arbayim], when the sun already inclines toward its setting. And so we say in the chapter [entitled] Amar Lahem HaMemuneh (Yoma 28b): The prayer of Abraham was from when the walls darken, which is from midday onward; and we learn from this that the slaughter of the daily offering begins from the seventh [hour]. And we raised a difficulty there [from] the Mishnah, [which states] that the daily offering is slaughtered at six and a half hours; and we answered: The walls of the Temple were different, as they were not straight — [they were] very wide at their base — and they do not darken until six and a half [hours].

Rashi on Pesachim 5a:17:1.hebrew: ואימא כל חד וחד - יבער סמוך לשחיטתו מעט, ואם שהה עד תשע — יבערנו בתשע:
Rashi on Pesachim 5a:17:1.english: And say: Each and every one - He should destroy [it] shortly before his slaughtering; and if he delayed until the ninth [hour], he should destroy it at the ninth [hour].

Rashi on Pesachim 5a:17:2.hebrew: זמן שחיטה קאמר רחמנא - לא חלקה תורה לישראל, לזה זמנו ולזה זמנו. הואיל וקבע לו זמן ואיסורו שוה בכל — לכולם זמן אחד קבע:
Rashi on Pesachim 5a:17:2.english: The Merciful One stated the time of slaughter - The Torah did not differentiate among the Jewish people, [giving] this one his time and that one his time. Since It established a [fixed] time for it and its prohibition applies equally to all, It established a single time for all of them.

Rashi on Pesachim 5a:19:1.hebrew: שהיא אב מלאכה - וזו הבערה שלא לצורך היא, והכתוב אסר מלאכה ביו"ט. הלכך, האי ראשון — בארבעה עשר קאמר:
Rashi on Pesachim 5a:19:1.english: That it is a primary category of labor - And this kindling is not for a [food] need, and Scripture prohibited labor on Yom Tov; therefore, this “first” is speaking of the fourteenth [of Nisan].

Rashi on Pesachim 5a:1:1.hebrew: השבתת שאור לאכילת חמץ - משעה שהזהיר שלא לאכול חמץ, צוה להשבית השאור, דכתיב: ״שאור לא ימצא בבתיכם כי כל אוכל (חמץ)״:
Rashi on Pesachim 5a:1:1.english: The removal of leaven to the eating of leavened bread - From the time that the Torah warned not to eat leaven, it commanded to remove the leaven, as it is written: “Leaven shall not be found in your houses, for whoever eats (leaven)”:

Rashi on Pesachim 5a:20:1.hebrew: אך חלק - התיר לך הכתוב לשהותו מקצת יום ביעורו. ואי יום ביעורו ביום טוב, מי שרי לשהוייה כלל? הא איתקש כו', ואכילת מצה משחשיכה, ועל כרחך השבתת שאור כשתחשך. ואם כן, לא משכחת "אך חלק". דאי לאו אך, איכא למימר: "ביום הראשון" — בין השמשות, שהוא התחלת היום; אבל השתא, על כרחך בתוך יום ביעורו שרי ליה קרא לשהוייה:
Rashi on Pesachim 5a:20:1.english: “Yet” divided - The verse permitted you to keep it for part of the day of its removal. And if the day of its removal were on the Festival [itself], is it permitted to keep it at all? Behold, [the removal of leaven] was juxtaposed, etc., and the eating of matzah is from nightfall, so perforce the removal of leaven [is required] when it grows dark; and if so, you cannot find [a case where] “yet” divided [the day]. For were it not for “yet”, it could be said: “On the first day” [means at] twilight, which is the beginning of the day; but now, perforce within the day of its removal, Scripture permitted one to keep it.

Rashi on Pesachim 5a:3:1.hebrew: ואכילת חמץ לאכילת מצה - משעה שחייב לאכול מצה, הזהיר שלא לאכול חמץ, דכתיב: "כל מחמצת לא תאכלו בכל מושבותיכם תאכלו מצות", וכתיב: "בערב תאכלו מצות". אלמא, זמן אכילת מצה ואיסור חמץ והשבתת שאור — משחשיכה:
Rashi on Pesachim 5a:3:1.english: And the eating of leavened bread to the eating of matza - From the time that one is obligated to eat matza, [the Torah] warned not to eat leavened bread, as it is written: “You shall not eat anything that is leavened; in all of your dwellings you shall eat matzot,” and it is written: “In the evening you shall eat matzot.” Evidently, the time of the eating of matza, the prohibition of leavened bread, and the removal of leaven [are all] from nightfall.

Rashi on Pesachim 5a:5:1.hebrew: אך חלק - אכין ורקין מיעוטין, אלמא מקצת היום מותר ומקצתו אסור. ומעתה, יש לנו לחלק חציו לאיסור וחציו להיתר. ואיכא דאמר: אך הוא חץ בגימטריא דאח"ס בט"ע גי"ף דכ"ץ, ותופס ח' תחת אל"ף וצד"י במקום כ':
Rashi on Pesachim 5a:5:1.english: “Yet” divides - [The words] akhin and rakin [“yet” and “only”] are restrictions; hence, part of the day is permitted and part of it is forbidden. And now [that we know it is divided], we must divide half of it for the prohibition and half of it for permission. And some say: “Akh” is [equivalent to] “khetz” [half] in the cipher of AChaS BeTa GiF DaKaTZ, taking [the letter] chet in place of alef and tzadi in place of khaf.

Rashi on Pesachim 5a:6:1.hebrew: ראשון דמעיקרא משמע - בלאו רומיא דקרא אהדדי, משמע ראשון במשמעות דקרא שהוא יום קודם לכל שבעה דקרא. כיון דכתיב: ״שבעת ימים מצות תאכלו אך ביום הראשון״ — ״ראשון״ קודם למעשה קאמר:
Rashi on Pesachim 5a:6:1.english: Rishon means previous - Without juxtaposing the verses against each other, rishon implies, according to the sense of the verse, that it is a day prior to all seven [days mentioned in] the verse. Since it is written: “Seven days shall you eat unleavened bread, but on the first day [you shall eliminate leaven from your houses]” — [the word] “first” means prior to the event.

Rashi on Pesachim 5a:6:2.english: Were you the first man born - Were you born prior to Adam, the first man?

Rashi on Pesachim 5a:9:1.hebrew: הכא נמי הא כתיב - בהאי קרא גופיה שבעת ימים, ודרוש נמי: ראשון דומיא דשביעי:
Rashi on Pesachim 5a:9:1.english: Here too, behold, it is written - In this very verse itself [it says,] “seven days,” and derive as well: “First” is similar to “seventh.”

Tosafot on Pesachim 5a:11:1.hebrew: למעוטי חולו של מועד - אתרווייהו קאי, דלולב אינו ניטל במדינה אלא יום אחד:
Tosafot on Pesachim 5a:11:1.english: “To exclude the intermediate days of the Festival” - [This] applies to both of them, as the lulav is taken in the province for only one day.

Tosafot on Pesachim 5a:14:1.hebrew: כדתנא דבי ר' ישמעאל - אע"ג דכתיבי טובא, בהנך ג' מצות כתיבי כולהו, וכל הכתוב במצוה אחד חשיבי חדא. ואין להקשות: מנלן דמהני ג' "ראשון" דרשינן, ו"אך ביום הראשון" לכדדרשינן? דילמא ההוא איכתיב להך דרשא! דמסתברא דמהני דכתיבי במקרא קודש דרשי' כולהו להך דרשא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 5a:14:1.english: "For that which the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught" - Even though [the word rishon] is written many times, they are all written regarding these three mitzvot, and all [occurrences] written regarding one mitzvah are considered one. And one should not ask: From where do we know that we expound [the teaching of Rabbi Yishmael] from these three [instances of] "rishon," and [expound] "However, on the first day" for that which we expounded [earlier]? Perhaps that [verse] was written for this exposition! For it is logical that from those [verses] that are written in [connection with] a sacred convocation, we expound all of them for this exposition.

Tosafot on Pesachim 5a:16:1.hebrew: לא תשחט את הפסח ועדיין חמץ קיים - הקשה רשב"א: היכי יליף מהכא דחמץ אסור מו' שעות ולמעלה? והא זמן שחיטת הפסח אחר התמיד הוי, ותמיד ששחטו לפני חצות פסול, וא"כ זמן שחיטה לא הוי מיד אחר חצות עד כדי שהיית הקרבת תמיד! וי"ל: כיון דדיעבד אם שחט הפסח קודם תמיד כשר, כדתנן התם, חשיב זמן שחיטה מחצות ואילך:
Tosafot on Pesachim 5a:16:1.english: "You shall not slaughter the Paschal lamb while leavened bread is still intact" - The Rashba [Rabbeinu Shimshon ben Avraham] asked: How does [Rava] derive from here that leaven is prohibited from six hours and onwards? For behold, the time of slaughter of the Paschal lamb is after the daily offering [tamid], and a daily offering that was slaughtered before midday is invalid; and if so, the time of slaughter is not immediately after midday, until [the passage of] the amount of time needed for the offering of the daily sacrifice! And one can say: Since after the fact (be-di'avad), if one slaughtered the Paschal lamb before the daily offering it is valid, as we learned in the Mishnah there, it is considered the time of slaughter from midday and onward.

Tosafot on Pesachim 5a:17:1.hebrew: זמן שחיטה קאמר רחמנא - אע"ג דאמת הוא ד"לא תשחט על חמץ" כל חד וחד כי שחיט, דאמרינן בפרק תמיד נשחט (לקמן פסחים סג. ושם): "השוחט את הפסח על החמץ עובר בלאו" — מ"מ, כיון דאשכחן דהזהיר על ההשבתה והזהיר שלא לשחוט פסח על חמץ, סברא הוא שבזמן שחיטה הזהיר על השבתה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 5a:17:1.english: "The Merciful One stated the time of slaughter" - Even though it is true that [the prohibition of] "You shall not slaughter [the blood of My sacrifice] with leaven" [applies to] each and every person when he slaughters, as we say in the chapter [entitled] "Tamid Nishchat" (below, Pesachim 63a and there): "One who slaughters the Paschal lamb with leaven violates a negative commandment" — nevertheless, since we find that [the Torah] warned regarding the destruction [of leaven] and warned not to slaughter the Paschal lamb with leaven, it stands to reason that it warned regarding destruction at the [general] time of slaughter.

Tosafot on Pesachim 5a:18:1.hebrew: דברי ר' ישמעאל - תימה לר"י: דתנא דבי רבי ישמעאל נפקא ליה מקרא אחרינא; ובכמה דוכתין פריך מר' ישמעאל אתנא דבי רבי ישמעאל:
Tosafot on Pesachim 5a:18:1.english: "The statement of Rabbi Yishmael" - It is puzzling to the Ri, for the Tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael derives it from another verse; and in several places [the Gemara] raises an objection from Rabbi Yishmael against the Tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael.

Tosafot on Pesachim 5a:19:1.hebrew: (ואומר) כל מלאכה לא תעשו - אע"ג דכשישרף ויעשה גחלים הנאתו מותר, כדאמר בפרק כל שעה (לקמן פסחים כו:) גבי ערלה: בישלה על גבי גחלים, דברי הכל הפת מותר, וה"ה חמץ; והא דתנן בפ' כל שעה (ד כא.): "לא יסיק בו תנור וכירים" — היינו מדרבנן. אור"י, דסברא הוא דקרא דתשביתו מיירי בכל ענין, אפילו אינו צריך לגחלתו. אי נמי, כיון דמתחלת הבערה אינו יכול להנות ממנו, אע"ג שיהא לו הנאה ממנו אחר כך — אסור; כמו נדרים ונדבות שאין קריבין בי"ט למ"ד (ביצה דף יט כ.), אף על פי שיש בהן מאכל הדיוט לבסוף, ומאן דשרי — שרי מלהנות:
Tosafot on Pesachim 5a:19:1.english: (And it says) "You shall perform no manner of work" - Even though when it is burned and becomes coals, benefit from it is permitted — as [the Gemara] says in the chapter [entitled] Kol Sha'ah (below, Pesachim 26b) regarding orlah: [If] one cooked [bread] over coals, all agree that the bread is permitted; and the same applies to leaven; and that which we learned in the Mishnah in the chapter [entitled] Kol Sha'ah (21a): "One may not fire an oven or a pot-range with it," that is [only] rabbinic — Rabbeinu Yitzchak says: It is logical that the verse "you shall remove" applies in all cases, even [where] one does not need its coals. Alternatively, since from the beginning of kindling one cannot derive benefit from it, even though one will derive benefit from it afterward, it is forbidden — like vows and freewill offerings, which are not offered on Yom Tov according to the one who says (Beitzah 19b–20a) [that they may not be offered] even though there is [food for] human consumption in the end; and the one who permits [them], permits [it because of the] benefit [derived in the end].

Tosafot on Pesachim 5a:1:1.hebrew: דהא איתקש השבתת שאור לאכילת חמץ וכו' - בפרק כל שעה (לקמן פסחים כח:) יליף ר' יהודה לאוכל חמץ מו' שעות ולמעלה שהוא בלא תעשה, ור' שמעון פליג עליה. ומהכא לא מצי למילף מידי, דלא הוקשה אכילת חמץ להשבתת שאור שמשש שעות ולמעלה, אלא להשבחת שאור של שבעת ימים. וקשה לרשב"א: אמאי לא יליף כרת להשבתת שאור מדאיתקש לאכילת חמץ:
Tosafot on Pesachim 5a:1:1.english: "For the removal of leaven is juxtaposed to the eating of leavened bread, etc." - In the chapter [entitled] Kol Sha'ah (below, Pesachim 28b), Rabbi Yehuda derives that one who eats chametz from six hours and onward [violates] a negative commandment, and Rabbi Shimon disagrees with him. And from here he could not derive anything, as the eating of chametz was not juxtaposed to the removal of leaven from six hours and onward, but rather to the removal of leaven of the seven days. And the Rashba raises a difficulty: Why does [the Gemara] not derive karet for the removal of leaven from [the fact] that it is juxtaposed to the eating of chametz?
